audited_suspected_testing_frame: 98 students admitted as typhoid cases during a known outbreak; active case-finding across 3,313 students
specimen_scope: BLOOD culture only (n=92), stated verbatim; Widal serology on all 98. No stool, urine or bone marrow
case_definition_summary: No standalone syndromic definition. Confirmed = fever >=3 days + positive blood culture; probable = fever >=3 days + positive serodiagnosis without isolation; possible = admitted on clinical suspicion during the outbreak. The effective frame is admission during a known outbreak
testing_selection_mechanism: NEAR-UNIVERSAL, NOT severity-gated. All 98 were admitted to the same military hospital; all 98 had Widal; 'Ninety two blood cultures were taken' (93.9%). The paper does not say why 6 were not cultured. No severity, consent or capacity gate described
temporal_alignment: No epidemic curve printed, though the text references a time-distribution graph showing multiple peaks
denominator_compatibility: COMPATIBLE and the best available: a stated blood-only tested count over a syndromic frame, with 93.9% coverage
source_status: primary paper reviewed (Zotero DVZCQ6W9); MJAFI 2008;64:241-242
simple_model_status: eligible: 5/92 with a stated blood-only denominator and 93.9% coverage
verification_model_status: candidate: lowest verification-bias risk of ANY outbreak study located in this project
audit_notes: THE FIND. 93.9% of suspected cases blood-cultured - better coverage than all three current anchors (Aye 44.9%, Neil 9.4%, Kabwama 3.6%). Positivity 5/92 = 5.4% implies pi ~0.09 at Se_BC 0.62, FAR below Aye 0.26 / Neil 0.58 / Kabwama 0.25. TWO COMPETING EXPLANATIONS THE MODEL CANNOT SEPARATE: (a) genuinely low pi because the denominator is loose - 86/98 were 'probable' on Widal alone at 1/160 H, 1/200 O, so the frame is closer to 'febrile children admitted during an outbreak' than a typhoid syndrome; (b) antibiotic-depressed Se_BC - the authors attribute the low yield to prior antibiotic therapy. Also: the paper reports the same 5 cases as 5.43% (of 92) in the text and 5.10% (of 98) in Table 1.

DO NOT use 42 as a blood numerator. Population 4,700; implied attack rate 18.4%; no deaths. Paper has several internal contradictions (Table 1 ALT >2xULN 12 < ALT >5xULN 13, impossible; ciprofloxacin n=17 in text vs n=15 in Table 2).

audited_suspected_testing_frame: 27 guests meeting the typhoid syndromic definition, out of a 147-guest retrospective cohort

source_status: primary paper reviewed (Zotero ED36QT97, attached by JK 2026-07-16 and verified). Supersedes JEMF2WZ7 and AW7IPIVI, which BOTH still contain Borgdorff 2001 (M. tuberculosis) via an OUP volume 152/154 same-page collision
audit_notes: CORRECTS MY EARLIER READING: the 15 'confirmed by stool or blood culture' CAN be split - 'S. typhi was isolated in six stool cultures and in 14 blood cultures (five cases with both cultures positive)'; 14+6-5=15. So blood-positive = 14, not an unsplittable pooled 15. Ineligible anyway because the blood-tested count among the 27 is never given. Cohort: 199 identified, 157 (79%) interviewed, 147 (94%) analysed. Gastroenteritis 133 (90.5%); typhoid 27 (18.4%); ALL typhoid cases had preceding gastroenteritis. Strong age gradient: typhoid attack rate 42% (16-19y), 32% (20-29y), 9% (30-39y), 0% (>=40y) - the authors read this as lower population immunity in the young in a low-endemicity country. 21/27 hospitalised, 2 severe (ICU 23d and 38d). Single phage type DVS / ribotype TP7, fully antibiotic-sensitive. NOTE: Koh excluded this study as 'no time-series data available', yet Figs 1 and 2 ARE epidemic curves. A plausible explanation is that the reviewers downloaded the OUP link and received the Borgdorff TB paper, as both prior library copies did.

audit_notes: CONCEPTUALLY THE MOST USEFUL REVIEW FOUND. Independently quantifies, across 68 outbreak studies spanning 1965-2019, exactly the scarcity supplement S9 asserts: only 15/68 (22%) reported ANY case definition; only 25/68 (37%) reported any laboratory-confirmation information; only 20/68 (29%) mention blood culture at all; only 3/25 (12%) defined what 'laboratory-confirmed' meant. Headline conclusion: 'No standardized case definitions or laboratory methods were reported.' Table 2 catalogues clinical signs across the 15: Fever (13), Abdominal pain (10), Diarrhea (10), Vomiting (8), Headache (7), Constipation (6). NOTE: the review EXTRACTED 'number of cases based on culture confirmation, serological testing and/or clinical suspected' and then never reported a single result for it. Many internal inconsistencies (41 vs 43 source studies; three incompatible control-strategy figures; Table 3 sums to 26 of 25) - cite the headline percentages, not the tables.

audit_notes: THE FIND OF THE RE-REVIEW, and it is a review - the category I had been dismissing wholesale. Tables 2-3 give screened denominator, inclusion criteria, positive cultures and % S. Typhi across 27 studies, STRATIFIED BY EXACTLY THE VERIFICATION AXIS: '(a) unselected populations with minimal selection criteria; (b) selected groups ... for example, investigation of only those with prolonged fever and a clinical diagnosis of possible typhoid fever; (c) case-series'. BLOOD-ONLY rows with denominators: Wain 1998 Vietnam 369/515 = 71.7%; Vollaard 2004 Indonesia 88/1019 = 8.6%; Brooks 2005 Bangladesh 49/889 = 5.5%; Crump 2003 Egypt 19/449 = 4.2%. POOLED rows needing source recovery: Bhutta 1999 46/97 (blood+BM), Ammah 1999 44/200 (blood+stool), Nizami 2006 40/214 (26 BC + 16 PCR; BC-only 26/214 = 12.1%), Cheesbrough 1997 11/120 (blood+stool). WAIN 1998 VALIDATES THE PROPOSED EXCLUSION RULE: 71.7% EXCEEDS Se_BC 0.62, so pi>1 is required - and its definition explains why (fever >=6 days + no obvious focus + negative malaria smear + abdominal discomfort + changed bowel habit). These are ENDEMIC FEVER SURVEILLANCE, so they expand the SURVEILLANCE stratum, not the outbreak anchors. WATCH: Crump 2003 Egypt (19/449) may be the same programme as Srikantiah 2006 Egypt (90/1815) already in the stratum. Also quotable: Vollaard 2005 'no symptom and sign combination performed adequately to be useful in clinical practice for identifying typhoid'.
